bib.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization

read.skipped: Appendix A proof text only skimmed; figures 10-26 are image-only so only captions read

question: How does the true (gold) reward change as a policy is optimized against an imperfect proxy reward model, and how does this scale with RM size, RM data, policy size, optimizer and KL penalty?
hypothesis: Optimizing a proxy reward model too far hurts the true objective (Goodhart's law), following a predictable functional form in sqrt(KL).
contributions: Empirically validated functional forms for gold RM score vs d=sqrt(KL) for best-of-n and RL
Smooth (approx. logarithmic) scaling of the coefficients with proxy RM parameters
Findings on RM data size, policy size, RL vs BoN and KL penalty
Discussion of implications for RLHF, iterated RLHF and the Goodhart taxonomy

method.summary: A synthetic setup in which a fixed 6B gold RM labels comparisons used to train smaller proxy RMs; policies (GPT-3 series, SFT on InstructGPT demonstrations) are optimized against the proxy by PPO or best-of-n, and the gold score is tracked against KL from the initial policy. Functional forms are fitted to the curves.
method.task: reward model overoptimization measurement (RLHF, InstructGPT environment)

datasets.name: Synthetic comparisons labelled by gold RM
datasets.size: 100,000 comparisons (RM data sweeps use up to 90,000 for training)
datasets.split: 10% held out as test set for validation loss
datasets.source: pairs of policy rollouts to the same prompt, higher gold score always marked preferred
datasets.preprocessing: RMs recentred so initial policy mean reward is 0; gold scores unit-variance normalised; proxy RMs recalibrated by rescaling logits on soft-label validation set

models.name: Gold RM
models.architecture: GPT-3 architecture with scalar head (the 6B RM of Ouyang et al. 2022)

models.name: Proxy RMs
models.params: 3M to 3B (12M and 1.2B and 3B used in particular sweeps)

other.excluded: two RMs smaller than 3M reached near-chance accuracy and were off-trend, excluded

models.name: Policies
models.init_from: pretrained GPT-3, SFT 2 epochs on InstructGPT demonstrations

training.objective: RM: pairwise preference loss on synthetic comparisons (inferred from 'validation loss'/'cross-entropy'); policy: PPO against proxy RM, or best-of-n selection (no training)
training.lr: RM Adam learning rate multiplier 1.67e-2; RL Adam learning rate multiplier 4e-3
training.epochs: SFT 2 epochs; RM 1 epoch (4 epochs tested in a control)
training.regularisation: KL penalty 0 for all RL experiments except section 3.6
training.seeds: not stated; 'most points ... already averaged over multiple seeds'

inference.decoding: BoN: sample n, pick highest proxy RM score
inference.samples: n up to 1,000 for fitting, up to 60,000 for validation; unbiased estimator of Nakano et al. 2021 App. I for intermediate n

metrics.name: Gold RM score
metrics.definition: score of the 6B gold RM on policy outputs, recentred to initial policy mean 0

metrics.name: KL
metrics.definition: D_KL(pi || pi_init); analytic for BoN, measured for RL

metrics.name: Proxy-gold gap
metrics.definition: proxy RM score minus gold RM score

baselines: best-of-n vs PPO against each other
eval.protocol: Fit R_bon(d)=d(alpha-beta d) and R_RL(d)=d(alpha-beta log d) to gold curves; advance prediction for BoN to n=60,000; extrapolation tests from low KL (Fig 26)

results.claim: BoN gold reward follows R(d)=d(alpha-beta d) with d=sqrt(KL).
results.setup: InstructGPT environment, GPT-3 policy 1.2B, proxy RMs 3M-3B, gold RM 6B

results.claim: RL gold reward follows R(d)=d(alpha-beta log d).
BoN functional form validated by an advance prediction out to n=60,000 (KL about 10 nats) having fitted data only to n=1,000 (about 6 nats).
results.quote: we performed a BoN experiment with up to n = 60, 000 (KL ≈10 nats), after

results.claim: alpha_RL can be held constant across RM sizes, leaving a clean scaling curve for beta_RL.
results.quote: we ﬁnd that we can hold αRL constant across all RM sizes

results.claim: RM data below about 2,000 comparisons gives almost no improvement over near-chance loss.
results.quote: for amounts of data less than around 2,000 comparisons

results.claim: Unique data matters more than SGD steps: 4 epochs of the same data gives no gold-score change, but 1 epoch of 4x data is substantially better.
results.quote: running 4 epochs instead of 1 yields no

results.claim: Larger policies gain less from optimization but overoptimize about as much; gold score peaks at almost the same KL for 1.2B and 6B policies.
results.quote: we ﬁnd that both gold scores peak at almost the same KL

results.claim: RL is far less KL-efficient than BoN: BoN KL grows about log(n), RL KL grows approximately quadratically with step without KL penalty.
results.quote: KL increases approximately quadratically with step in

results.claim: A KL penalty does not move the KL-gold frontier; its effect is akin to early stopping (result may be hyperparameter sensitive).
results.quote: does not affect the KLRL-gold reward frontier

results.claim: Peak BoN gold score predicted in closed form as alpha_bon/(2 beta_bon).
results.quote: Max BoN gold scores (αbon/2βbon) predicted with the BoN closed form

results.claim: Iterated RLHF with k iterations raises final gold score by beta_RL * d * log k under additive-d and constant-coefficient assumptions.
Authors attribute the nonmonotonic gold score and the beta term mainly to extremal Goodhart; alpha term reflects regressional Goodhart.
results.quote: We expect extremal Goodharting to be primarily responsible for the nonmonotonicity

results.claim: Answer-length exploitation by optimized policies is a real issue seen in other InstructGPT-setting experiments.
results.quote: Optimized policies producing very long answers even when a short answer would be preferred is a real issue

limits: Synthetic gold RM stands in for humans; transfer to real human labels untested and RMs may be correlated
Does not capture mismatch between human labels and true human intent (Sec 4.5)
Single InstructGPT environment; only two policy sizes; mostly default PPO hyperparameters; KL-penalty result may be hyperparameter sensitive
Proxy scores poorly fit; RL form has infinite slope at origin
Adversarial Goodhart not captured; trends may break for more capable models
Number of RL steps, seeds, compute and hardware not stated; no code release stated
Data-threshold result contradicts some internal findings (fn 8)

terms.definition: Optimizing too much against such a model eventually hinders the true objective
fixed 'gold-standard' reward model playing the role of humans
